Index: go.sum
===================================================================
--- go.sum	
+++ go.sum	
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+golang.org/x/text v0.42.0 h1:JbOZXgfeCPU9gacVtYliJqOhD+zhrEqK4LfdpmlUZqI=
+golang.org/x/text v0.42.0/go.mod h1:ojzP1Z+2QtioaF8DTtO8K5q7JWVVYwZKenzujK0Zd0E=

Index: main_test.go
===================================================================
--- main_test.go	
+++ main_test.go	
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+package main
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestRun(t *testing.T) {
+	tests := []struct {
+		name     string
+		from, to string
+		form     string
+		in, want []byte
+		wantErr  bool
+	}{
+		{
+			name: "nfc composes combining marks",
+			form: "nfc",
+			in:   []byte("e\u0301"),
+			want: []byte("\u00e9"),
+		},
+		{
+			name: "nfd decomposes",
+			form: "nfd",
+			in:   []byte("\u00e9"),
+			want: []byte("e\u0301"),
+		},
+		{
+			name: "latin1 to utf-8",
+			from: "latin1",
+			to:   "utf-8",
+			form: "none",
+			in:   []byte{0xe9},
+			want: []byte("\u00e9"),
+		},
+		{
+			name: "utf-8 to latin1",
+			from: "utf-8",
+			to:   "latin1",
+			form: "none",
+			in:   []byte("\u00e9"),
+			want: []byte{0xe9},
+		},
+		{
+			name:    "unknown source encoding",
+			from:    "bogus",
+			wantErr: true,
+		},
+		{
+			name:    "unknown normalization form",
+			form:    "bogus",
+			wantErr: true,
+		},
+	}
+
+	for _, tt := range tests {
+		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			if tt.to == "" {
+				tt.to = "utf-8"
+			}
+			var got bytes.Buffer
+			err := run(tt.from, tt.to, tt.form, bytes.NewReader(tt.in), &got)
+			if tt.wantErr {
+				if err == nil {
+					t.Fatalf("run() = nil error, want error")
+				}
+				return
+			}
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("run() error = %v", err)
+			}
+			if !bytes.Equal(got.Bytes(), tt.want) {
+				t.Errorf("run() = % x, want % x", got.Bytes(), tt.want)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

No remote. I'll name the module something sensible. Since it's an app handling text encoding conversions and Unicode normalization, I'll call it `textconv`. Module path could be `example.com/textconv` or just `textconv`. Since no remote, I'll use `textconv`. Actually best practice: use a domain-like path if it might be imported. Since it's an app (main package), a simple module name is fine. I'll use `textconv`.

The app needs `golang.org/x/text` for encoding conversions (charmap, unicode etc.) and Unicode normalization (golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm).

- go.mod
- main.go with a small app
- maybe go.sum after go mod tidy
